# Matías Montero

<p class="standfirst">How relationships and institutions shape educational opportunity</p>

I am a **DPhil researcher in Education at the University of Oxford**, funded by the UK’s Economic and Social Research Council. My work examines how gender, institutional prestige, and social ties shape academic careers and educational trajectories.

::: {.agenda}
## Connecting structures, relationships, and outcomes

My research moves across higher education, schools, and classrooms, using longitudinal and relational methods to understand when institutions reproduce inequality — and when they create room for change.

<ol class="index-list">
<li>
<span class="index-num">01</span>
<div>
<h3>Academic careers</h3>
<p>How gender and institutional prestige influence collaboration, research funding, leadership, and attrition across education researchers’ careers.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<span class="index-num">02</span>
<div>
<h3>Educational transitions</h3>
<p>How stratified systems shape course choices, higher-education access, and the trajectories of migrant and international students.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li>
<span class="index-num">03</span>
<div>
<h3>Relational methods</h3>
<p>How social network analysis and quantitative research can reveal the mechanisms linking opportunity structures to educational outcomes.</p>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
:::

::: {.spread}
::: {}
<p class="kicker">Current doctoral work</p>

## Networks and gender disparities across academic careers

My DPhil investigates the formation and persistence of gender disparities in Latin American education research. I model co-authorship and funding networks over time to examine how individual careers and institutional contexts interact.

<p class="more-link">[View research projects](projects.qmd)</p>

<p class="kicker">Featured publication</p>

## Gender segregation in secondary-school course choices

This <em>American Educational Research Journal</em> article examines socioeconomic gradients and the protective role of school gender culture in Chile.

<p><strong>Ortega, Montero, Canals &amp; Mizala (2025)</strong></p>
